frontier.name: The kernel of `G → G ⧸ N`.
frontier.text: Over a field, with `G` geometrically reduced, the projection is faithfully flat. It remains to show its kernel is exactly `N`, so that `G ⧸ N` represents the fppf quotient. Results on how rational points permute the weight spaces of `N` begin the usual argument.

frontier.name: Representable quotients `G/H`.
frontier.text: Chevalley's theorem is in place and the fppf quotient sheaf exists. What remains is representing it by a scheme, via the orbit of the stabilized line, and showing it is affine when `H` is reductive.

frontier.name: Conjugacy of Borels and root data in general.
frontier.text: Conjugacy is known for `GLₙ` and `SLₙ` only. A general version is needed to extract the root datum of an arbitrary reductive group. The normalizer of a torus now acts on its characters through a finite group, but identifying `N(T)/T` with the Weyl group is still open.

frontier.name: The unipotent radical.
frontier.text: It remains to prove that the connected normal smooth unipotent subgroup is maximal in general. The present criteria only recognise it.

frontier.name: Reductivity of the remaining carriers, and the pinned isomorphism theorem.
frontier.text: The spin, tripled `D₄` and `E₆` carriers have trivial unipotent radical when reduced. Each still needs to be identified with the smooth connected subgroup its root subgroups generate. The existence half of the pinned isomorphism theorem and a uniform construction from root data are also missing.

frontier.name: Classical Koszulity of zigzag algebras.
frontier.text: Extend the exact Koszul complex beyond its second stage and prove Koszulity exactly off finite ADE. The non-Dynkin Hilbert series of Layer 4 and the inverse-Cartan comparison of Layer 3 depend on this.

frontier.name: Self-injectivity of ADE preprojective algebras.
frontier.text: Finite-dimensionality is now known for all types, but self-injectivity only for `A₁` and `A₂`. The named `D₄` and `E₈` are the next cases.

frontier.name: Braid relations.
frontier.text: Prove that the complexes `B_i` and `B_i'` are mutually inverse, commute for nonadjacent vertices and satisfy the braid relation for adjacent ones, then compute the action on graded `K₀`.

frontier.name: Liu–Wang formality.
frontier.text: Prove that the affine `D₄` deformation is nontrivial up to `A∞` isomorphism, then establish the Hochschild comparison and the intrinsic-formality theorem for trees. This needs derived Koszul duality for `Π₂(Q)`, which has not begun.

status.glance: Layers 0–2 are done. Layers 7 and 8 have their first constructions, Liu–Wang's affine `D₄` `A∞` deformation and the braid complexes, but none of their theorems.

frontier.name: Ladder operators on `L²`
frontier.text: : `a` and `a†` exist only on Schwartz space. On `L²` they are unbounded, so extending them needs closed-operator packaging rather than continuous linear maps. The README treats this as a downstream target, not a milestone.

frontier.text: : out of scope by design. The roadmap assigns them a separate future roadmap, and the families would have to be defined before any `L²` basis statement about them.

status.glance: Every part of the roadmap is done. The Hermite functions and the Chebyshev polynomials are complete orthonormal bases of their `L²` spaces. Both are built from one family-agnostic layer that also gives the weighted-measure and multidimensional bases. Each basis carries an explicit expansion and Parseval API. The Hermite basis also has its two main structural consequences: it diagonalizes the `L²` Fourier transform, and on Schwartz space it carries the ladder operators. What is left lies outside the roadmap's own targets.

frontier.name: Higher homotopy of spheres and `RPⁿ`.
frontier.text: The covering isomorphism gives `π_k(RPⁿ) ≅ π_k(Sⁿ)` for `k ≥ 2`, but nothing here computes `π_n(Sⁿ)`; that needs a degree or Hurewicz argument, and neither appears here.

frontier.name: Existence of `K(G, 1)` spaces for an arbitrary group.
frontier.text: Only recognition is proved, with circles and tori as examples; constructing one for a given group rests on realization theory the README places outside this roadmap.

frontier.name: Bases without a universal cover.
frontier.text: The standing local hypotheses are shown to be exactly what a simply connected cover requires, so the classification cannot be pushed further as stated; spaces failing them would need a different notion of cover, and nothing here attempts one.

status.glance: Every stage of the roadmap has its stated targets proved. The universal cover is constructed, subgroups of `π₁(X, x₀)` classify connected covers in both pointed and unpointed form, covers are classified categorically with `π₁(X, x₀)` recovered as the automorphisms of the fibre functor, and the application list (`π₁(S¹)`, `π_n(S¹)`, tori, `K(G, 1)` recognition, `RPⁿ`) is complete. What remains lies beyond the roadmap's text: computing higher homotopy groups, and bases without a universal cover.
